topic: Servo load, holding torque, current, receiver brownout, flutter practice, simulator servo practice and product-name use for the servo load plan (D6-SRV)
note: Guide: docs/research/servos/D6-SRV-00/README.md. Local copies in the gitignored references/servos/d6-srv-00/ (reference only, do not redistribute). Web-only sources are listed with url and no path. Dead ends: gear-strip torque versus stall torque by gear material (no manufacturer or measured source after 4 searches), back-drive torque (not a typical specification), thermal/overload trip thresholds and timing, receiver reboot times outside Spektrum, MIL-A-8870C numeric free-play limit (paywalled), any RC simulator modelling servo torque, blowback, brownout or flutter, servo-editor documentation for RealFlight 7 through Evolution, Phoenix, ClearView, neXt and PicaSim.

files.use: 4.8 / 6.0 V: 0.28 / 0.23 s/60 deg no load; stall 11 / 13.2 kg.cm; standing torque 8.8 / 10.5 kg.cm at 5 deg hold-out (80 % of stall); idle 8 mA; running 230 / 250 mA; stall 1500 / 1800 mA; dead band 5 us; cored metal-brush motor. Speed, torque and stall current all rise 1.20x for a 1.25x voltage ratio.

6.0 V: stall 0.45 N.m, rated 0.15 N.m; stall current 0.68 A, rated 0.25 A; no-load 0.13 s/60 deg, rated 0.20 s/60 deg; rated voltage 3.8-8.4 V. The linear torque-speed line predicts 0.195 s/60 deg at the rated point.

files.kind: manufacturer manual (Horizon Hobby, DSMX receiver, retailer mirror)
files.use: Minimum operational voltage 3.5 V; below 3.5 V the system ceases to operate; with the transmitter on it reconnects typically in about 0.04 s; most servos cease below 3.8 V; Brownout Detection not available in DSMX mode.

files.kind: manufacturer user guide (Horizon Hobby, DSM2 receiver, 2009, third-party mirror)
files.use: QuickConnect reconnects typically within a second; below 3.5 V a reboot can take several seconds (cold start 2-6 s); power-system test: voltage should remain above 4.8 V with all servos heavily loaded.
Power requirement 3.7-7.4 V (voltage range 3.5-8.4 V). No reboot time found.

Report No. 45 simplified flutter criteria for VD below 260 kt EAS, derived statistically from full-size airplanes: aileron K/I balance and wing torsional flexibility limits versus VD, aileron free play below a specified maximum, elevator/rudder dynamic balance, tab free play at most 2 % (tab span up to 35 %) or 1 % of tab chord. Applicability to RC scale not established.

files.kind: NACA technical note (Martin 1958), as served by NTRS in a container wrapping 19930085030.pdf
files.use: Crude criteria for wing bending-torsion and stall flutter of missile lifting surfaces; control surfaces are only discussed qualitatively. Not a control-surface flutter criterion.

files.kind: commercial simulator manual (Knife Edge / Great Planes)
files.use: Physical servo editor exposes SERVO SPEED (s per 60 deg) only; BRAKE SERVO STRENGTH applies to wheel brakes. Flight Failures (reverse, stuck, trim, channel swap, lockout, interference, range) are probability events, all enabled by default. No load-dependent servo behaviour.

servoclassic moves toward the target with a given Speed; electrical_actuator has InputVoltage, MinimumVoltage, RatedCurrent and AddLoad, with no torque effect on motion described. Use by Aerofly RC 10 unverified.

Slop is the greatest contributor to flutter at high speed; longer servo horns accentuate gear slop. Qualitative.
Static balancing of control surfaces is usually the best remedy. Qualitative.
